description: Triage register for @trailofbits/vsix-audit findings on the roo-plus VSIX. Every entry is a finding that a maintainer has characterized as by-design (content coincidence, bundled OSS, data/prose/source-map/grammar/WASM bytes, or declared capability). When run on demand (it is NOT wired into any publish pipeline), scripts/vsix-audit.mjs fails closed on any finding NOT listed here, on any severity/count escalation above the recorded baseline, and on degraded coverage (YARA-X unavailable) in a publish context. See SECURITY.md 'Optional on-demand VSIX audit' + DEBT #23.

scan.note: Full-coverage baseline (YARA-X present) of the 3.87.3 artifact. Not re-scanned by any pipeline; regenerate this file when a maintainer runs a deliberate on-demand pass and triages new or changed findings.

remap.reason: Issue #13 webview chunk consolidation renamed the hashed webview chunks (and Sub-task B Curated Shiki removed the common-lisp grammar).
remap.method: DETERMINISTIC REMAP (no re-scan). The register tool resolves (@trailofbits/vsix-audit@0.3.0 via npx) but YARA-X is not installed, so a full-coverage scan cannot be reproduced; regenerating would have produced degraded coverage. Each entry keyed to a hashed webview chunk was re-pointed to the current build file carrying the same module identity, resolved from the production source maps. Where several old chunks collapsed into one new chunk, their counts were summed (the gate only fails when findings EXCEED the recorded count, so a summed cap is conservative).
remap.limitation: Filename-level remap only: rules/severities are carried over unchanged from the last full-coverage scan (3.87.3), so this is NOT a re-verified scan. A maintainer must regenerate with YARA-X present before relying on it as a fresh baseline. The scan.* block still describes the original 3.87.3 full-coverage scan.
remap.regeneration: MUST be regenerated with @trailofbits/vsix-audit (pinned 0.3.0) WITH YARA-X (v1.20.0) present before this register is treated as a fresh baseline; a YARA-X-less run is degraded coverage and must never be recorded as a baseline (scripts/vsix-audit.mjs fails closed on that in a publish context). The register is FILENAME-KEYED: every entry's `file` must equal the scanner's reported path, so any webview rebuild that re-hashes chunk names (or adds/removes a chunk) invalidates the affected entries and the gate FAILS CLOSED until they are re-mapped or re-scanned. The `file` for the YARA_STEALER_JS_Credential_File_Exfil_Jan25 finding was corrected from `changelog.md` to the packaged `CHANGELOG.md` (the pack ships the uppercase name and the scanner preserves case). See SECURITY.md 'Optional on-demand VSIX audit' + DEBT #23.
